description: This small data set gives approximate water intake locations for 62 thermal power plants in the Western Interconnection (WECC) power grid. It was published on Zenodo in June 2020 by Kristian Nelson, Sean Turner and Nathalie Voisin of Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, with support from the US Department of Energy Water Power Technologies Office. For each plant it records geographic coordinates of the cooling water intake, and it adjusts the plant coordinates given in the Union of Concerned Scientists EW3 energy-water database so that the water transfer distance between plant and intake can be calculated. A README describes the fields. Coverage is the Western Interconnection. Files are a CSV table and a text README, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: intake locations are approximate, only 62 plants are included, and the data have not been updated since 2020. Simulation uses are linking thermal plants to river flow and water temperature models to assess curtailment risk under drought and heat. Related records: data-us-federal-hydropower-projections-cmip5 covers climate effects on western hydropower.
